claim: On 2026-08-13 ACM announced that existing public certificates can switch from email to DNS validation without reissue or a new ARN, with up to 72 hours to add the DNS records; before, the ACM guide said that an email-validated certificate cannot switch to DNS validation and must be deleted and requested again.

values.display: you cannot switch to validating it with DNS

evidence.heading: AWS Certificate Manager supports switching from e-mail to DNS validation

evidence.quote: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) now enables you to change the domain validation method on your existing ACM issued public TLS certificates from e-mail to DNS, without reissuing the certificate or changing its existing Amazon Resource Name (ARN).

ACM provides a CNAME record for each domain in the certificate (the same mechanism used when provisioning new certificates with DNS validation) and you have up to 72 hours to add the records to your DNS configuration.
After you create a certificate with email validation, you cannot switch to validating it with DNS. To use DNS validation, delete the certificate and then create a new one that uses DNS validation.
